parties:
Shushil Chandra Nath ----- Appellant
Vs.
Shanjib Kanti Nath and anr ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
9. The learned Counsel for the respondent raising question as to the maintainability of the suit referred to the relief sought in the suit. The plaintiff prayed for "That a decree be passed in favour of the plaintiff declaring the alleged deed of gift executed on 14-1-73 and registered on 18-4-73, false, fabricated, fraudulent, collusive, illegal and inoperative in law". The learned Counsel submits that both the Courts, appellate Court as well as trial Court, wrongly allocated burden of proof to the defendant, that the appellate Court misread the judgment of the trial Court since there is nothing in the judgment of the trial Court that PW 2 by mistake stated the signature of Mohendra Kumar Nath in the deed of gift is of Mohendra Kumar Nath. It may be mentioned it was submitted on behalf of the appellant that, in fact, what PW 2 stated was that he doubted the signature of Mohendra Kumar Nath in the deed of gift. The learned Counsel for the respondent continued that courts below misread the evidence of PW 2 who stated “আমার দাদুর দস্তখত চিনি। নালিশী দানপত্রে মহেন্দ্র কুমার নাথের দস্তখত তাহার নিজের।” The learned Counsel submits that the point for determination in the suit is, whether the deed of gift was a forged one and that the burden of proving the said fact is on whom. The learned Counsel submits that it being possible for the plaintiff to establish the genuineness or otherwise of the deed of gift because of availability of thumb impression of Mohendra Kumar Nath but he having had not done so the courts below were in error in not holding that plaintiff failed to discharge his onus of establishing that the deed of gift was not a genuine one. The learned Counsel has further submitted that plaintiff having had not discharged his burden the trial Court as well as the appellate Court were in error in placing the burden on the defendant to prove the genuineness of the deed of gift, although the deed of gift was a registered one and because of that there was a presumption of correctness of the entry made in the deed of gift, that PW 2 being one of the members of the family of Mohendra Kumar Nath and he having had admitted that signature of Mohendra Kumar Nath appearing in the deed of gift is of Mohendra Kumar Nath and that his statement being not a contradictory one nor denial of the statement made earlier, the trial Court as well as the appellate Court were in serious error in discarding the evidence of the said witness for no cogent reason and the appellate Court was in error in discarding the evidence of PW 2 on the view that trial Court held the said evidence of PW 2 mistaken one although the trial Court did not hold anything like that about the evidence of PW 2. It has been submitted by the learned Counsel that whatever evidence plaintiff had brought on record relating to the deed of gift was negative in nature and that the evidence of the PWs. does not show Mohendra Kumar Nath did not execute the deed of gift. It may be mentioned here that as regard the statement of PW 2 relating to signature of Mohendra Kumar Nath appearing in the deed of gift it has been submitted by the learned Counsel for the appellant that on the basis of single statement of PW 2 which is contrary to the evidence of other witnesses it cannot be said that the deed of gift is a genuine one. The learned Counsel further submitted that it will be best to read the statement as quoted herein-before to the effect "নিজের মনে হয়" instead of in the affirmative i.e. that the signature of Mohendra Kumar Nath in the deed of gift is of Mohendra Kumar Nath. The learned Counsel for the appellant has also taken exception as to non deposing by defendant No. 2 and there-upon submits that adverse presumption may be drawn in the background of the said fact as to the genuineness of the deed of gift and the learned Counsel has referred to the case of Sardar Gurbakhsh Singh vs Gurdial Singh and another reported in AIR 1927 (PC) 230 wherein it has been observed that party to the suit should be offered as witness. In the back-ground of the facts of the instant case, we are of the view that the defendant No. 2 as had no interest in the land in suit, as such, because of his non examination as a witness by the defendant No. 1 it cannot be considered or presumed that he (defendant No. 2) did not depose to avoid telling the truth about the deed of gift. The learned Counsel for the respondent raised the question of maintainability of the suit. We are of the view the question of maintainability need not be dealt with by us in disposing of the appeal since the plaintiff by reliable evidence has not established the fact alleged by the plaintiff for having the relief sought in the suit. 

 10. It is seen from the judgment of the High Court Division as well as of the courts below that plaintiff was in control of the thumb impression of Mohendra Kumar Nath. The document in question i.e. the deed of gift, being a registered document thumb impression of Mohendra Kumar Nath was also available in the thumb impression register of the office of the Sub-Registrar. The plaintiff could have obtained the experts opinion in respect of the thumb impression appearing in his kabala and the thumb impression appearing in  the deed of gift on the basis of the thumb print maintained by the office of the Sub-Register in its thumb impression register but he having had not done so we are of the view defendants part of establishing the genuineness of the deed of gift which is a registered one upon dislodging the evidence brought on record by the plaintiff did not arise. It is seen from the judgment of the lower appellate Court and the trial Court that in spite of the fact that the plaintiff did not discharge his duty of establishing that the deed of gift is a non-genuine one the said Courts saddled the defendant with the burden of establishing that the deed of gift was a genuine one. It is also seen that the appellate Court as well as the trial Court without considering the evidence of PWs 1 and 5 held that the plaintiff is in possession of the land in suit. It is seen from the evidence on record that PWs 1 and 5 admitted possession of the defendant. The lower appellate Court as well as the trial Court also lost sight of the fact that deed of gift was of earlier date than that of the kabala on the basis of which plaintiff claiming the title of the land in suit. In that state of the matter, it was the bounden duty of the plaintiff to establish non-genuineness of the deed of gift and that plaintiff having had not done so, in spite of having had the opportunity to do so, we are of the view the High Court Division has quite legally set aside the judgment of the courts below. It is seen from the evidence on record that the PWs except making general statement that Mohendra Kumar Nath did not execute the deed of gift and that the evidence of PWs being negative in nature relating to the execution and registration of the deed of gift by Mohendra Kumar Nath we are of the view High Court Division was not in error in setting aside the judgment of the lower appellate Court affirming the judgment of the trial Court.
